structure.text: Werther's letters let the relationship grow through his selection of incidents, feelings, and interpretations.

structure.title: A narrowing perspective
structure.text: Later letters and editorial framing place the intensity of his account beside information that he cannot fully organise for himself.

context.title: Letters as perspective
context.text: A letter gives access to feeling but not an impartial account of everyone involved. Werther decides what becomes evidence.

context.title: Feeling and social position
context.text: Frustration concerns rank and work as well as love. Werther's sense of exclusion has several sources.
context.takeaway: Keep the wider world around the attachment visible.

notice.text: Notice changes in descriptions of nature.
notice.why: The landscape registers shifts in his inner life.
Her life exceeds the meaning Werther assigns it.

opening: Werther meets a woman looking after her younger siblings and falls in love with the whole scene. Lotte is warm, intelligent, and already promised to someone else. Knowing that does very little to change what he feels, and his letters turn every meeting into evidence that this attachment has become the centre of his life. Goethe makes the intensity seductive enough to inhabit, while allowing the reader to see how a person can gradually organise an entire world around a desire it cannot satisfy.
